name: Mana-zone
tagline: A web app in the trading card game orbit: deck building and collection tracking, going by the name and the domain.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The public footprint here is thin, so treat this as a judgement about the category rather than about a specific feature list. Card game tooling sits on top of card data that is already free and open: Scryfall publishes every Magic card, every printing, every image URI, with no key and a permissive bulk download. Once the data is a solved problem, a personal deck builder and collection tracker is a search box, a join table, and a mana curve chart. A coding agent can do that in one sitting and it will feel fine because you are the only user. What you will not reproduce in a sitting is the polish layer: price history, format legality nags, import from every other tool, and a mobile view you actually enjoy using at a shop table.
coreLoopDIY: Search a local copy of the card corpus, add cards to decks and to a collection, and see curve, color, and legality stats plus what you still need to buy.
requirements: Scryfall bulk data download, free, no API key, respect the rate limits
A local SQLite file for decks and collection
whatYouLose: Price data and market history, which is the part that is genuinely someone else's dataset
Importers for the dozen formats other deck sites export
A mobile experience that survives one handed use in a card shop
Sharing: public deck links, comments, and anyone else seeing your lists
Someone else keeping up with new set releases and banlist changes
moatNotes: The card corpus is open. Card images and prices are not, and that is where the paid tiers in this category usually live.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the annoying parts are the parts nobody wants to maintain: set releases every few weeks, format legality that changes on a schedule someone else sets, price feeds, and a scanner that reads a physical card without making you type. A personal build handles the part you find fun and quietly rots on the rest. If you only build decks for yourself and do not care what they cost, the paid version is optional. If you trade, sell, or play sanctioned events, the upkeep is the product.
notes: Open card data means the hard part is already done for you; the maintenance treadmill is what you are actually paying to avoid.
prompt:
Build a local-first deck builder and collection tracker for Magic: The Gathering in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, one file at ./data/app.db, no ORM.
- No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud. Single user on localhost.

Data:
- Write scripts/import-cards.ts that downloads the Scryfall "default_cards" bulk JSON, streams it, and inserts into a cards table: id, oracle_id, name, set_code, collector_number, mana_cost, cmc, type_line, oracle_text, colors (json), color_identity (json), rarity, image_uri_normal, legalities (json).
- Create a FTS5 index on name, type_line, oracle_text.
- Cache the download in ./data/cache so reruns are cheap. Set a descriptive User-Agent. Do not hammer the API.

App:
- /search: query box, results as a virtualized grid of card images with name and set. Filters for color identity, type, cmc range, rarity, format legality.
- /collection: quantity owned per printing, foil flag, add and remove inline, total card count.
- /decks: create, rename, delete decks. Deck page has mainboard and sideboard, quantities, 4-copy warning, legality check against the deck's chosen format, mana curve bar chart, color pip breakdown, and a "missing from collection" list.
- Plain text import and export in the standard "4 Lightning Bolt" format. Resolve names against the local cards table, report unmatched lines instead of failing silently.

Explicitly out of scope: prices, card scanning, sharing links, other games, users, deploy config.

Deliver a README with setup steps, a seed command, and the exact import command. Put nothing in .env because nothing here needs a secret.
